item.title: Exact dimer ground states of long-range spin chains and ladders
item.description:
📚 Phys. Rev. B
👤 Jędrzej Wardyn and Miłosz Panfil
Author(s): Jędrzej Wardyn and Miłosz Panfil This work establishes necessary conditions for the exact dimer ground states in a wide class of spin chain models with arbitrary long-range interactions. The stability of the dimer phase is also probed by introducing an anisotropy or dimerisation with the analytical findings supported by the numerical computations. The considered models encompass physical phenomena ranging from spin-Peierls materials to dimer state implementations in quantum information processing. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 264414] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026

item.title: Conductivity of a non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid: Exact solution of the kinetic equation
item.description:
📚 Phys. Rev. B
👤 Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov
Author(s): Tatia Kiliptari, Vladimir I. Yudson, and Dmitrii L. Maslov In a Fermi liquid, the quasiparticle scattering rate scales as T 2 , whereas the low-temperature correction to the residual resistivity can scale as T 4 , seemingly implying a strongly suppressed current-relaxation rate. The authors resolve this paradox here by solving the kinetic equation exactly for a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid. They show that electron–electron collisions enter the conductivity through the quasiparticle scattering time itself, which controls the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic transport. The extra T 2 factor arises because momentum conservation makes the change in the total velocity of two colliding electrons vanish on the Fermi surface, so current relaxation come…

item.title: Signatures of Gaussian superconducting fluctuations in nonlocal noise magnetometry
item.description:
📚 Phys. Rev. B
👤 Dror Orgad
Author(s): Dror Orgad Are superconducting fluctuations in a film above its transition temperature dominated by short-lived Cooper pairs or by vortices? Here, the author calculates the magnetic-noise correlations sensed by two spatially separated diamond quantum probes, considering the film both in equilibrium and under an applied electric field. The distinct relaxation scales and directional patterns of the noise offer a means of distinguishing between the two scenarios. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 264511] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026
